rationale: F10 is the right next step for five reasons. First, the collection-centric pivot is a natural evolution validated by the POC: only 3 of 548 collection cards matched existing DB data, proving that the generic set-based backfill strategy (F01/F04/F08) collected data the user does not actually need. Pivoting to collection-driven sync aligns data collection with actual user value. Second, the existing infrastructure is well-suited: the MYP provider already has curl_cffi with rate limiting, retry, and Cloudflare bypass (F01); the search API at /produto/search?marca=magic&term={query} provides the lookup mechanism to find MYP product IDs for collection cards; batch upsert and asyncio concurrency are proven (F04); and the collection importer, UserCollectionRow model, and collection API endpoints already exist from the POC. Third, cleaning the database is a low-risk operation because the old data can be re-backfilled at any time using the existing backfill CLI/API — the infrastructure is preserved, only the data is removed. Fourth, upgrading Scryfall images to HD (art_crop or large instead of normal) is a trivial URL parameter change in the existing _scryfall_image_url helper. Fifth, F09 (scheduled collection) was planned but not shipped, and its value proposition changes fundamentally under the collection-centric model — instead of scheduling generic set updates, the scheduler would update only collection cards, making F09 a natural follow-up to F10 rather than a prerequisite. The plan-feature action is correct because this is a multi-concern feature (DB cleanup, new sync pipeline, image upgrade, frontend adjustments) that requires Architect decomposition into properly sequenced tasks.
risks: MYP search API may not return results for all 548 collection cards — name mismatches between CSV (English names) and MYP (Portuguese-centric catalog) could cause low match rates, leaving many collection cards without price data
DB cleanup removes all historical price observations — if the user later wants to analyze cards outside their collection, that data is permanently gone unless re-backfilled

Search-based matching is inherently fuzzy — cards with common names, reprints across sets, or special editions (foil, promo, alternate art) may match the wrong MYP product, leading to incorrect price tracking
Rate limiting against MYP search API — 548 cards x 1 search each at 1s delay = ~9 minutes minimum, and failed searches may need retry, extending the initial sync window

F09 scope invalidation — the planned F09 (cron + health endpoint) was scoped for generic set-based collection; F10 changes the collection model, so F09's PRD and decision record (D-20260819-002) become partially stale
mitigations: Implement a two-phase matching strategy: (1) exact match by set_code + collector_number in existing source_cards, then (2) MYP search API fallback for unmatched cards. Log match confidence and allow manual review of ambiguous matches

Before cleanup, export a DB backup (SQLite file copy) and document the re-backfill procedure. The backfill infrastructure (CLI + API + provider) is preserved — only data rows are deleted, not schema or code

For search-based matching, use set_code + collector_number as disambiguation keys when multiple MYP results are returned. Store the match confidence/method on the source_card so the user can audit questionable links

Use the existing asyncio.Semaphore concurrency (default 3) for parallel search requests, with the proven rate-limiting and retry-on-429 logic from MypCardsProvider._fetch(). Estimate and display progress to the user

Mark F09's PRD and decision record as superseded-by-F10 in a future update. The health endpoint and cron concepts from F09 remain valid but should be re-scoped after F10 ships to target collection-only sync

existing_infrastructure: MypCardsProvider with curl_cffi, rate limiting, retry, concurrency
UserCollectionRow model + repository methods (list, count, summary, sets)
Collection API router (list, summary, sets, import)
MyCollection.tsx frontend page with image tiles, search, filters, pagination
Collection CSV importer with canonical card linking
Batch upsert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
Scryfall image URL helper (currently using 'normal' quality)
